title: Run determined by the first $t$ choices
statement: Let $\mathrm{run}$ map Boolean words to configurations, and let $\mathrm{halted}$ be a predicate on configurations. Suppose that whenever a run on $w$ is halted, appending any word $w'$ to $w$ leaves its result unchanged. Suppose also that every word of length $t$ produces a halted result. Then for every word $w$ with $t\le |w|$, its prefix of length $t$ has length $t$, produces a halted result, and has the same run result as $w$.
hypotheses_covered: A function from Boolean words to a type of results
A predicate on results expressing that they are halted
Appending any word to a halted run leaves its result unchanged
Every Boolean word of length $t$ produces a halted result
